instruction: Could you help me add all the changes in the current project and create a commit with the message "first commit" from the command line?

command: git config --global user.name "xlang" && git config --global user.email "xlang2024anonym@gmail.com" && mkdir -p /home/user/projects/remote_project && cd /home/user/projects/remote_project && git init --initial-branch=main && git config receive.denyCurrentBranch ignore
unzip -q /home/user/Downloads/binder.zip -d /home/user/projects/ && cd /home/user/projects/binder && git init --initial-branch main && git remote add origin /home/user/projects/remote_project

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to add all changes and create a commit with message 'first commit'. Evaluator checks git log output contains the commit message 'first commit'. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric and vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts state: 'git log --oneline | head -n 1' retrieves the most recent commit message, which is exactly what needs to be verified
Metric logic is appropriate: check_include_exclude correctly verifies that 'first commit' appears in the git log output
Complete coverage: The evaluator verifies the final outcome (commit exists with correct message), which implicitly confirms both requirements (git add + git commit) were completed successfully
Expected value is correct: 'first commit' matches the exact requirement in the instruction
Practical verification approach: A commit cannot be created without staged files, so verifying the commit message implicitly confirms files were added
